ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; FINTRAC Guidance and Interpretation Notices; Limited Partnership Act, SBC 2021, c 22, and Limited Partnership Regulation, BC Reg 271/2022 (partner registers, records office, and UBO records); Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 (corporate general partner registers); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, as amended by the Budget Implementation Act, 2023 (federal beneficial ownership registry); Land Owner Transparency Act, SBC 2019, c 23 (BC transparency reporting when the LP owns land); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 21; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp.) partnership reporting provisions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BC Corporate Registry or the equivalent corporate registry of the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Global Affairs Canada, Canada party effective 14 January 2024); Consular Legalization only for non-Hague Convention origin documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or authorized director of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada, or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified passport copies for each individual beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization; apostille of the notarial certificate where the KYC file is used internationally

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's reference / credit and solvency letter for the general partner and each 25%+ limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized banker's certificate (no apostille required for the internal AML file; apostille available for foreign banking counterparty KYC)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney and corporate resolution appointing the BC registered office / attorney for service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the resolution and POA

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / criminal record certificate for natural-person general partners and senior management
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RCMP-certified police records or applicable national police authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable to the issuing state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant customer due diligence: (1) identify and verify every general partner, every limited partner holding at least 25% of the limited partnership, and any controlling person; (2) screen against the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, Canada's autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Criminal Code terrorist entity list, the OFAC SDN List (required for USD rails cleared through US correspondent banks), and, where contractually engaged, HM Treasury and EU sanctions lists; (3) screen domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and their family members and close associates, with enhanced measures for PEPs; (4) run ongoing transaction monitoring on the B2B SaaS billing rails (Stripe Billing and Wise B2B), including Large Cash Transaction, Electronic Funds Transfer, and Suspicious Transaction Reporting to FINTRAC as applicable; (5) document UBO tracing through the registers of every intermediate holding entity until natural persons holding more than 25% are identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services - Corporate Online (https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca), operated by the Corporate Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services; cross-checked via the Canadian OneStop Business Registration portal for the CRA Business Number.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory rules under the Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, and the Limited Partnership Act, SBC 2021, c 22: a BC limited partnership name must contain (i) a distinctive element, (ii) a descriptive element, and (iii) a legal element ending with 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', the French form 'Société en commandite', or the abbreviations 'S.E.C.' or 'SEC'; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name, must not be scandalous or imply an illegal undertaking, and must be in English, French, or both; where the name is in a non-Latin script, an English or French transliteration is required; corporate forms such as 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.' may not be used by a limited partnership; statutory filing forms are processed in English and French, and a foreign general partner's name must appear in its original and transliterated form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name approval issued by the BC Corporate Registry is valid for 56 days; the limited partnership must complete registration within that window or file a new Name Request (no statutory extension of the initial window exists, although a fresh reservation may be purchased). Upon rejection: (1) the applicant reviews the rejection reasons in Corporate Online and resubmits a revised Name Request with a supporting argument and any consents, trademark registrations, or evidence of prior use; (2) if the rejection persists, the applicant files a written administrative reconsideration with the Manager, Name Approvals, attaching a due-diligence report distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting names and proving an absence of confusion with existing BC or national records; (3) if the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241, within prescribed time limits, or alternatively select a new distinctive and descriptive name and refile.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the ISIC 6201 B2B SaaS sub-sector. The Limited Partnership Act, SBC 2021, c 22, requires the LP to maintain a registered office in British Columbia capable of receiving service of process and a separate records office in British Columbia where the partner register, UBO records, and statutory books are kept. A licensed BC corporate service provider's physically attended office, or a virtual office suite open during business hours that accepts process service, satisfies the registered-office mandate; a P.O. box alone does not. The low-risk SaaS business model does not require a local lease, employees, or commercial substance beyond the registered and records offices, because the partnership is tax pass-through and licensing/API revenues are intangibles-based; however, the records office must be able to present registers on demand to FINTRAC, the CRA, and the Registrar.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 10% probability of any unannounced physical inspection during the initial 24-month operating period. BC Registries does not routinely conduct physical visits of LP registered offices; verification is usually by written correspondence. CRA and FINTRAC examinations for a low-risk SaaS entity with Stripe and Wise payment rails are predominantly desk-based; unannounced site visits are reserved to high-risk, cash-intensive, or sanctionable activity, or where a service-of-process claim or auditor red flag arises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (CAD 20, converted at 1 CAD = 0.74 USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary NUAMS computerized name search and conflict screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BC Registries online service through licensed service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the limited partnership (initial registration under the Limited Partnership Act, SBC 2021, c 22)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and records office retainer with licensed BC corporate agent (24-month initial term)
Notarized KYC bundle: general partner resolution, incumbency certificate, certified passports, legal status proofs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the jurisdiction of origin of the documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication of three origin documents (Global Affairs Canada, post-14 January 2024 accession)
UBO piercing, PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening, and AML/CFT compliance file assembly (formation counsel fixed fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Canadian business law firm / corporate counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pass-through partnership and IRC Section 7701 check-the-box tax classification opinion for Canada-US SaaS revenues
CRA Business Number (BN) and GST/HST registration application

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, Part 3 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 44-86; Limited Partnership Regulation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Registrar of Companies, Government of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership filed with the Registrar of Companies; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a British Columbia limited partnership. Limited partners' capital contributions are contractual and do not require a statutory escrow account. The general partner must be identified in the declaration, and capital contributions may be in cash, property, or services as agreed in the limited partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the General Partner of [●] Limited Partnership: 1. The Limited Partnership Agreement dated [●] is adopted, and the initial limited partners in Schedule A are admitted with the capital subscriptions stipulated. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address, British Columbia], and [●] is appointed BC registered agent for service. 3. [●] is authorized to sign and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with BC Registries and to obtain the Certificate of Limited Partnership. 4. [●] is authorized, jointly or singly, to sign tax registrations, bank instructions, and commercial agreements for the Limited Partnership. 5. This resolution is effective immediately and all prior acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Name Search and Corporate Registry agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search report through BC Corporate Online or a licensed BC Registry agent. If the proposed name requires approval, submit a Name Reservation Request and include fall-back names. The name must contain 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' as a legal element and must not contain prohibited words. No notarization is required for the name search. Retain the name reservation number for the filing.
required_dossiers: Priority search report if name contains a distinctive element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects on the ground of confusing similarity, file a substitute name reservation within the response period stated in the notice; the reservation fee is generally non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft limited partnership agreement and governance pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and legal counsel; no government filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement covering capital contribution requirements, allocations of profits and losses, management powers of the general partner, limited partner veto rights, transfer restrictions, and dissolution provisions. Record the General Partner's written resolution in lieu of board minutes. If premises are leased for the registered office, obtain landlord consent to use the address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No external filing is made at this stage; amend the draft to reflect partner comments before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — BC Corporate Online (Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online using a registered BC Registries account. Select 'Limited Partnership Registration' and complete the Declaration of Limited Partnership. List at least one general partner and one limited partner, the BC registered office, and the mailing or records address. Ensure the declaration is signed by the general partner and confirm that limited partner contributions are agreed. Pay the filing fee online; no notarization is required for online filings.
required_dossiers: Consent to appointment of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, respond to the Registrar's requirement letter within the stated period through BC Corporate Online; if the filing lapses, re-file with a new declaration and applicable fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Limited Partnership and establish statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership with the registration number and effective date. Download the certificate from BC Corporate Online, place it in the statutory records, and establish the partners' register and minute book. If the limited partnership will carry on business in other Canadian provinces, arrange extra-provincial registration where required.
required_dossiers: Partnership minute book or statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a certified copy of the certificate through a BC Registry search and pay the applicable copy or search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax and statutory accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Ministry of Finance; WorkSafeBC if employees are engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Business Registration Online portal to obtain a Business Number for the limited partnership. Register for GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed or will exceed the CRA threshold, for BC PST if the LP sells taxable software or meets non-resident vendor registration triggers, for payroll if employees are engaged, and for WorkSafeBC coverage if a physical office is operated in British Columbia. Each registration is made in the name of the limited partnership with the General Partner as contact.
required_dossiers: General Partner's identification and Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Business Registration Online rejects the application, verify the partnership type code and General Partner Business Number, then file a paper RC1 form with the CRA. If GST/HST registration is not mandatory, document the reason in the tax file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licensing department of the registered-office municipality; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a physical office is maintained, apply for the municipal business licence in the locality, e.g. a City of Vancouver business licence. Provide the Certificate of Limited Partnership and lease or occupancy evidence. Arrange a fire safety inspection and secure an occupancy certificate for the office. Comply with WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety requirements if workers are engaged. If the LP operates entirely remotely with no BC premises, verify whether a home-office licence or no licence applies under the relevant zoning bylaw.
required_dossiers: Fire safety certificate (if premises are used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses a home-office licence, submit a zoning compliance letter and, if necessary, apply for a minor variance; alternatively, use a commercial registered-office address without onsite employees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no BC industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over ISIC 6201 software development; municipal business licensing is the only local licensing requirement that may apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for the core enterprise SaaS business; a general municipal business licence is the only operating authorization if a BC office is maintained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based software development does not constitute a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act; no registration or EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOCs, or regulated industrial emissions are generated in normal SaaS operations. General office waste and e-waste must be managed under the BC Recycling Regulation and applicable electronic stewardship programs; if future data-center hardware is deployed, waste electrical and electronic equipment handling must comply with BC Hazardous Waste Regulation thresholds and electrical safety standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety compliance is mandatory if employees work in British Columbia. A fire safety inspection and occupancy certificate are required for any office premise under the BC Building Code and Fire Code. No separate civil defense clearance is prescribed; leased server racks must satisfy structural load limits confirmed by the landlord and building engineering review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); national portal: CRA My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE. BC provincial retail sales tax (PST, 7%) is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance (eTaxBC); British Columbia does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST), so only the 5% federal GST applies in BC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The LP must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST Program Account (account type RT). Steps: (1) register the limited partnership under the BC Partnership Act via the BC Corporate Registry (OneStop BC); (2) apply to CRA through Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or the BC registry's one-stop data transfer; (3) CRA issues the BN and activates the GST/HST RT account upon mandatory registration or election. Mandatory registration arises when worldwide taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or C$30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA small-supplier rule); voluntary registration is available under ETA s. 240(2). For GST/HST purposes the partnership is deemed a person (ETA s. 272.1), so the GST/HST account is held in the LP's own name. Non-resident LPs may register directly with CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The LP is fiscally transparent under ITA s. 96; no entity-level federal or BC income tax is imposed on the partnership. Each partner includes its distributive share of Canadian-source income or loss in its own return; non-resident partners are taxable under Part I on their share of the LP's Canadian business income, and certain allocations may attract Part XIII withholding. The LP generally files Form T5013 (Partnership Information Return). For GST/HST, the same LP is a separate registrant and must file its own GST/HST returns, so income-tax fiscal transparency coexists with entity-level GST/HST compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a check-the-box entity classification regime. Relevant statutory elections: (i) ITA s. 96(3) - a partnership that is not a Canadian partnership but carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada may elect to be treated as a separate person resident in Canada, centralizing compliance for non-resident partners; (ii) ETA s. 273 - election among closely related registrants (including qualifying corporate partners and the LP) to treat certain supplies as made for nil consideration; (iii) ETA s. 240(2) - voluntary GST/HST registration for small-supplier LPs; (iv) the hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s. 18.4) operate mandatorily without election for cross-border arrangements exploiting deduction/non-inclusion mismatches.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; foreign exchange supervision administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential banking.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; no prior approval or exchange control license is required for profit remittance or capital repatriation by a British Columbia limited partnership, but distributions to non-resident partners are subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (generally 15% under the Canada-USA treaty, 25% otherwise, unless reduced by treaty).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Canada. Export receipts may be retained in any foreign currency; however, FINTRAC mandates reporting of all cross-border wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more per transaction, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) or Statistics Canada requires exporter declarations for certain goods (not applicable to software services).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise Business, Stripe Treasury, Airwallex) are feasible as supporting payment rails for customer collections and vendor payables, but they are not licensed as Canadian Schedule I or II banks under the Bank Act. They operate as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC and cannot provide a regulated deposit account for capital subscription proceeds or hold client trust funds. Legal constraints include Canadian anti-money-laundering (AML) rules, transaction volume caps, and the prohibition on taking deposits without a banking license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Canadian federal statute mandates physical presence of directors or partners for corporate account opening. Tier-1 Canadian banks generally permit remote video-identification KYC for domestic entities; however, for a British Columbia limited partnership with non-resident limited partners, banks may require (a) a registered office address in BC, (b) a notarized or apostilled certification of partner identity, and (c) a recorded interview with the general partner or authorized signatory. Without a Canadian resident director, additional due diligence is triggered under FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) and high-risk jurisdiction assessments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution from a non-resident private company in a jurisdiction with opaque corporate registries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified organizational documents, directorship and register of members, audited financial statements, bank reference letter from the remitting institution, commercial contracts explaining the source of funds, and a legal opinion on the non-criminal origin of the capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected incoming cross-border payments to the LP's operational account that could be mischaracterized as unlicensed money-service activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed B2B SaaS subscription agreements, usage and revenue reports, Stripe Billing and Wise transaction logs, a completed FINTRAC MSB self-assessment showing non-application, and legal counsel's memorandum confirming contract payment, not remittance services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the LP's declared tax pass-through status and its actual bank-account usage such as foreign exchange trading
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended limited partnership agreement, BC Registrar filing certificate, annual financial statements, CRA partnership information return (T5013), and a tax opinion confirming no active financial business beyond provision of enterprise software development.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: partner banks execute SWIFT MT103 using a valid ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., 'CUST' for capital settlement or 'DIVI' for profit distribution); complete beneficiary line includes the LP's legal name, BC limited partnership number, and Canadian Financial Institution Number; no mandatory surrender or pre-conversion applies. For wire transfers equal to or greater than CAD 10,000, the receiving bank must file an Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) with FINTRAC. Pre-verification includes submission of the capital call notice, partner resolution, and a signed source-of-funds declaration if requested.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlements require the use of the SWIFT network via MT103 for direct vendor payments, MT202 for bank-to-bank indemnity settlements, or documentary letters of credit under UCP600 for large purchase obligations. For domestic CAD payments, Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail (RTR) and the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) provide irrevocable clearing; for USD settlement against a Canadian bank account, the US Fedwire and CHIPS networks are used. B2B SaaS subscription payables and refunds may be processed through Wise or Stripe using automated clearing house (ACH) equivalents in the respective jurisdictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX Contract (delivery-based or cash-settled) for CAD/USD
Cross-Currency Swap (fixed-to-fixed or floating-to-fixed) with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank or OSFI-authorized counterparty
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) limited to illiquid currencies and executed through an OSFI-regulated financial institution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: British Columbia Limited Partnership Annual Report (renewal of registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of the limited partnership's initial registration date (anniversary-based cycle, not a fixed calendar date). Example: registration on 18 July 2025 triggers a first annual report deadline of 17 September 2026.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty approximately CAD 180 (approx. USD 132) in addition to the regular CAD 60 fee; continued non-filing leads to administrative strike-off and dissolution of the limited partnership under the BC Limited Partnership Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and T5013 partner slips with applicable schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T5013 return due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end; for the standard December 31 year-end, the deadline is May 31 of the following calendar year. T5013 slips must be distributed to partners and filed with CRA by the last day of February following the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty per Income Tax Act s. 162(7): CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; partner-level late-filing penalties and possible gross-negligence penalties apply for false or incomplete reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Significant Controllers (Beneficial Ownership) Confirmation filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registry Services, public beneficial ownership registry regime effective 16 May 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual report, within 2 months after each registration anniversary; any in-year change to significant controllers must be filed within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or knowingly filing false significant-controller information constitutes an offence under the BC transparency registry regime; recurring default may trigger administrative strike-off and significant monetary penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit is imposed on a British Columbia limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Act or Partnership Act. An independent audit is triggered when: (i) the partnership agreement mandates an annual audit; (ii) a senior secured lender, major institutional investor, or large B2B enterprise customer requires audited statements; (iii) the limited partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities laws; or (iv) CRA demands audited financial statements in connection with a tax audit. A private enterprise SaaS limited partnership with no public-market exposure typically operates without a statutory audit but commonly undertakes a less extensive annual review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP per the CPA Canada Handbook: ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is the default framework for a private Canadian limited partnership; IFRS is mandatory if the partnership is publicly accountable (reporting issuer). Financial statements must reconcile to GST/HST and BC PST filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under BC's transparency regime, the general partner must identify and confirm annually all individuals with significant control, generally defined as persons directly or indirectly holding or controlling at least 25% of partnership distributions or capital, or who control the general partner. The annual confirmation is delivered to the BC Registrar concurrently with the annual report; changes occurring during the year must be filed within 30 days. The former in-entity transparency register has been superseded by the public beneficial ownership registry (effective 16 May 2025), but supporting due-diligence records must still be retained at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners and Contributions (analogous to the Register of Members)
Register of General Partner Appointments and Changes (analogous to the Register of Directors)
